about.title:
Six Decades of
Faith & Service
about.p1: Founded in 1963, the Conseil Protestant du Rwanda (CPR) is the umbrella body uniting Rwanda's 25 Protestant churches. Since its inception, CPR has been at the heart of Rwanda's social fabric — rebuilding communities after conflict, championing education, and upholding the dignity of every person.
about.p2Start: Today, through its departments in education, health, evangelism, and communications, CPR touches every province of Rwanda. Our motto —
about.motto: “Bose Babe Umwe” (That All of Them May Be One)

whoWeAre.title: About Conseil Protestant du Rwanda
whoWeAre.p1: The Protestant Council of Rwanda (CPR) was established in 1963 to promote and share innovative development initiatives and deliver essential services to our member churches and the wider community.
whoWeAre.p2: We are committed to developing strong, impactful partnerships and providing world-class services to those we work with, fostering faith, unity, and sustainable development across Rwanda.

visionMission.missionDesc: To bring together Protestant churches in Rwanda for a coordinated impact in evangelization, education, health, and holistic socio-economic development.

departmentsPage.heroDesc: Seven strategic departments driving CPR's mission across education, development, finance, youth, gender, communications, and governance.
departmentsPage.introTitle: Departments of the Conseil Protestant du Rwanda
departmentsPage.introDesc: CPR's work is organized through seven specialized departments, each led by experienced professionals and supported by dedicated staff. Together, they implement programs that touch every province of Rwanda, from education and health to youth empowerment and community development.

cta.title: Partner with Our Departments
cta.desc: Whether in education, development, health, or youth empowerment — your organization can make a difference alongside CPR's dedicated departmental teams.

gs.title: General Secretary's Office
gs.desc: The General Secretary provides strategic leadership, coordinates all departmental activities, and represents CPR at national and international levels. This office ensures institutional coherence and alignment with CPR's mission and vision.
body: Strategic planning and institutional governance across all member churches
Coordination of the General Assembly, Executive Committee, and Bureau meetings
Official representation at government, ecumenical, and international forums
Legal affairs, human resources, and institutional communication
Partnership development with local and international organizations
Oversight of annual reporting, audits, and organizational performance

bnep.title: Bureau National de l'Éducation Protestante (BNEP)
bnep.desc: BNEP is the education arm of CPR, overseeing Protestant primary and secondary schools across Rwanda. With 595+ primary schools and hundreds of secondary institutions, BNEP shapes the future of Rwanda's children through quality faith-based education.
body: Supervision of 595+ Protestant primary schools and associated secondary schools nationwide
Participatory Active Pedagogy (PAP) training for teachers in modern classroom methods
Development of Protestant religious education curriculum for primary and secondary levels
School inspection, quality assurance, and educational standards enforcement
Early childhood education programs and teacher training colleges
Partnerships with REB, UNICEF, and international education donors

diakonia.title: Diakonia / Development
diakonia.desc: The Diakonia department coordinates CPR's social services, humanitarian relief, and sustainable development initiatives. It serves the most vulnerable communities through holistic programs that combine faith, practical support, and long-term empowerment.
body: Emergency humanitarian relief and disaster response coordination
Community development programs focusing on sustainable livelihoods
Psychotraumatology and trauma healing — certifying counselors nationwide
Water, sanitation, and health (WASH) initiatives in rural communities
Capacity building for church leaders in project management and administration
Partnerships with Bread for the World, FECCLAHA, and local NGOs

finance.title: Finance & Resource Mobilization
finance.desc: The Finance department ensures CPR's institutional sustainability through transparent financial administration, strategic resource mobilization, and rigorous oversight. It manages budgets, donor funds, and internal controls across all departments.
body: Budget preparation, monitoring, and financial reporting to stakeholders
Donor fund management and grant compliance for international partners
Internal audit, risk management, and financial control systems
Resource mobilization strategies including church contributions and external fundraising
Payroll, procurement, and asset management across all departments
Quarterly and annual financial statements for the Executive Committee and General Assembly

youth.title: Youth Program
youth.desc: The Youth Program empowers young Rwandans through faith-based leadership training, peacebuilding initiatives, and reconciliation projects. It creates platforms for youth to become active contributors to their churches, communities, and the nation.
body: Annual Youth Peace and Reconciliation Summits gathering youth from all member churches
Leadership development camps and vocational skills training programs
Digital evangelism and media training for young communicators
Anti-trauma clubs in schools promoting mental health awareness
Inter-church sports and cultural exchange programs
Scholarship and mentorship programs for outstanding young leaders

gender.title: Gender Promotion Department
gender.desc: The Gender Promotion department champions gender equality, women's empowerment, and the fight against gender-based violence (GBV) across CPR member churches and communities. It integrates gender perspectives into all CPR programs and policies.
body: Gender mainstreaming across all CPR departments and member church programs
GBV prevention and response training for church leaders and community workers
Economic empowerment programs for women — savings groups, cooperatives, and entrepreneurship
Women's leadership development and representation in church governance structures
Advocacy campaigns on women's rights and child protection
Partnerships with government gender machinery and international women's organizations

radio.title: Radio Inkoramutima 107.1 FM
radio.desc: Radio Inkoramutima ('Voice of the Heart') is the official radio station of the Protestant Council of Rwanda. Broadcasting since 2005 on 107.1 FM, it reaches communities across Rwanda with messages of faith, unity, healing, and development.
body: Daily broadcasts of devotional programs, sermons, and faith-based content
Community news, public announcements, and development messaging
Trauma counseling and mental health talk shows reaching rural listeners
Youth and women's programs promoting social cohesion and national unity
Live coverage of CPR events, synods, and national commemorations
Partnerships with other community radio stations and media development organizations

sgProfile.title: Secretary General, Conseil Protestant du Rwanda
sgProfile.quote: The Protestant churches of Rwanda are called to be one — to serve together, witness together, and build this nation together. CPR exists to make that unity visible and effective in every corner of Rwanda.

General Assembly sessions — the supreme governing body, convened annually with all 25 member churches

Strategic planning retreats — annual sessions to review and update CPR's five-year strategic plan

body: Implements resolutions of the General Assembly and Executive Committee
Represents CPR in national and international forums and ecumenical bodies
Coordinates all departments and ensures institutional coherence

Maintains official correspondence and institutional memory

radioPage.heroDesc: The official voice of the Protestant Council of Rwanda, reaching communities in every corner of the country with messages of faith, unity, and holistic development.
radioPage.introDesc: Radio Inkoramutima ("Voice of the Heart") is the official radio station of the Protestant Council of Rwanda. Born on 27 December 2012, the station broadcasts on 107.1 FM — uniting CPR member churches, spreading the Gospel, and promoting the holistic development and social welfare of Rwandan communities.

about.title: From a Long-Cherished Dream to Reality
about.desc: Many years before the Genocide against the Tutsi in 1994, the idea of a CPR radio kept returning in the discussions of CPR structural organ meetings — but it was never put into practice. The Ministry of Evangelism judged a radio communication tool relevant for spreading the Gospel to a great number of people across the country, the region, and the world.
body: At the beginning, CPR hired airspace on the national Radio Rwanda and started broadcasting evangelization messages for 30 minutes at a time.
CPR built a small studio at its head offices in Kicukiro, used by the Communication and Evangelization Department to prepare and edit evangelization programmes before they were aired on Radio Rwanda.

Protestant Sunday services were broadcast live by Radio Rwanda through two technical studios — one at the Saint Etienne cathedral of the Anglican Church of Rwanda (Diocese of Kigali) and the second at the Kiyovu parish of the Presbyterian Church.

In 2012, the CPR General Secretary, together with the Technical Staff team of the Mission and Church Mobilization Department and the support of radio technicians, conducted a study to establish Radio Inkoramutima.
On 27 December 2012, the dream of many years became a reality: Radio Inkoramutima was born.
Today the station operates 17 hours daily — from 5:00 am to 10:00 pm — from its premises at Kimihurura Sector, Gasabo District, Kigali.

vision.visionDesc: To unite CPR members in spreading the Gospel by fighting against false teaching and promoting the holistic development and social welfare of Rwandan communities in particular and the world in general.
vision.missionDesc: To inform, educate, and entertain the community in different sectors of national life.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.desc: Quick answers to the questions we hear most often.

items.q: How can my church become a member of CPR?
items.a: Membership is open to Protestant churches and Christian organizations in Rwanda that share our vision of unity and holistic development. Contact the General Secretariat and our team will guide you through the process.

items.q: How do I partner with CPR on a project?
items.a: We welcome national and international partners. Send us a message through the form or email partnerships inquiries to cprgs@cpr-rwanda.rw and our team will respond within 48 hours.

items.q: How can I support CPR's work?
items.a: You can support us through prayer, volunteering, or donations. Reach out to us and we will share the ways your contribution can make a lasting impact on Rwandan communities.

items.q: Can I request media coverage or an interview?
items.a: Absolutely. Our communications team handles media requests — including coverage of our events and interviews with our leadership. Contact us with the details of your request.

items.q: Where is the CPR head office located?
items.a: Our head office is located at KG 2 Av 4, B.P 79, Kigali, Rwanda — in the heart of the capital city.

cta.title: Prefer to Talk Directly?
cta.desc: Call or email us and a member of our team will be glad to assist you during office hours.
